ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the outer boundary is a horizontal rectangle AQRD, with the top side labeled A, P, B, Q from left to right, and the bottom side correspondingly labeled D, S, C, R. The vertical lines PS and BC divide the rectangle into three parts, and the middle vertical rectangle PBCS is shaded gray. This gray part is exactly the overlapping region of square ABCD and square PQRS inside rectangle AQRD. Reasoning: The side lengths of the two squares are both 15, so the area of each square is 15^2=225. The dimensions of the outer rectangle AQRD are 15 by 25, so its area is 15×25=375. The union of the two squares is exactly rectangle AQRD, so use inclusion-exclusion: 375=225+225-overlap area, so overlap area=225+225-375=75. The ratio of the shaded area to the area of the rectangle is 75/375=1/5=20%.

method.method_draft: Use an area inclusion-exclusion route. From the image, identify the shaded vertical rectangle as the overlap of square ABCD and square PQRS inside the larger rectangle AQRD. From the text, each square has side length 15, so each square has area 15^2=225, and the outer rectangle AQRD has dimensions 15 by 25, so area 375. Apply union area = area(square ABCD)+area(square PQRS)-area(overlap). Thus shaded overlap area = 225+225-375=75. The percent shaded is 75/375 * 100 = 20.

method.method_draft: Use horizontal lengths along the top of the diagram. From the image, the whole top edge AQ is split into AP, PB, and BQ, where PB is the shaded strip’s width. Square ABCD has top side AB=15, and square PQRS has top side PQ=15. The whole rectangle has AQ=25 from the text. Since PQ=15 and AQ=25, AP=25-15=10.
